proof_roadmap: Use normality to obtain the global major-premise spine constraints.
Identify the topmost assumption that persists in the final context.
Prune the first elimination and replace the labelled assumption through the spine.
Induct on fewer inferences and reconstruct the conclusion by a left rule, retaining weakening for bottom conclusions.
difficulty_reason: H2: obtaining a cut-free target requires a global analysis of the normal derivation rather than the ordinary rule translation that can use Cut. The author proves structural facts about its major-premise main spine, including absence of introductions and location of disjunction/existential elimination, then uses context persistence to prune the first elimination and replace the affected labelled assumption through the spine. This produces a strictly smaller derivation for induction, after which a left sequent rule reconstructs the required conclusion without Cut. The complete spine argument, pruning cases and empty-succedent/weakening conventions are retained; the previously counted N1i normalization theorem is not counted again.

editorial_notes: All mathematical statement and proof text is reproduced verbatim from the Open Logic Project, unit proof-theory, file translations.tex, fixed at commit 1e960beff9ed7835bf3e3f1335e21af3439cd107. Only the packaging (the adapter preamble and the standalone wrapper) is this module's.
Numbering inside this standalone excerpt is editorial, not the Open Logic Project print numbering.

The adapter preamble loads the project's OWN style layer verbatim (sty/open-logic-formulas.sty, sty/open-logic-tokenize.sty, sty/open-logic-selective.sty and open-logic-config.sty, including its tag truth assignment), so the author's !! text-token shorthand, !A math metavariables, rule names (Intro, Elim, FalseInt) and the tag conditionals resolve exactly as in the book. Three substitutions are forced by the pinned toolchain and are recorded: isomath.sty is absent so \mathsfit is \mathsf; xpunctuate.sty is absent and unused so its RequirePackage is dropped; thmtools/ntheorem are absent so the environments are amsthm with the project's family numbering. The proof trees are the project's own bussproofs-extra.

The H2 judgement and its reason were made in this module by reading the author's own statement and complete proof at the pinned line span. Original candidate key: proof-theory/normalization|translations.tex|prop:normal-N2i-to-G2i.

Reference labels in the proof resolve to navigation pointers to the original author source; these pointers do not reproduce proofs of the prerequisites. The author's own ollabel is kept unprefixed (not part:chapter:section) so those pointers resolve; the label text itself is the author's own argument.
